title: Mahan
capsule: Mahan (馬韓) was the largest of the three Han confederacies of ancient Korea, comprising some fifty-four chiefdom-level polities across the Han River basin and the modern Gyeonggi, Chungcheong, and Jeolla provinces. Politically dominant among the Samhan peoples as early as the third century BCE, it was coordinated by the paramount chieftain of Mokji, located near present-day Cheonan. One of Mahan's own constituent statelets, Baekje, grew in military power and began progressively absorbing the others; by the late third century CE only about twenty Mahan polities remained. Baekje completed the conquest by the early fifth century, making Mahan's territory the heartland of one of the Three Kingdoms of Korea.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Mahan is known primarily through the Chinese Wei Zhi (third century) and later Korean compilations; boundaries of individual chiefdoms are conjectural and the overall territory's limits remain debated among Korean and Chinese archaeologists.
